title: 11-year-old boy dies after Galle Face drowning incident
byline: An 11-year-old boy has died following a drowning incident at Galle Face on Wednesday evening (10), where six children were swept away by strong sea currents while bathing along the beachfront.

title: Heavy rain, strong winds forecast today
byline: Sri Lanka is expected to experience widespread showers, strong winds and isolated heavy rainfall today (11), the latest weather forecast issued by the Meteorology Department ​said.

title: Iran says it struck ships in Strait of Hormuz after US launches new strikes
byline: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) says it has struck ships in the Strait of Hormuz, after the US military launched a new wave of strikes on Iran.

title: Iran announces closure of Strait of Hormuz after US attacks
byline: Iran’s top ​joint military ‌command announced the closure ​of ​the Strait of ⁠Hormuz ​on Thursday, ​including oil tankers and commercial ​ships, ​saying any vessel ‌that ⁠will attempt passage will ​be ​shot ⁠at.

title: Canada proposes teen social media ban - with workaround for tech firms
byline: Canada is proposing a social media ban for children and teenagers under the age of 16, mirroring a similar law passed in Australia late last year.

title: UNDP urges SL to regularise carbon markets to unlock private capital
byline: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has urged Sri Lanka to urgently operationalise and regularise its policy position on carbon trading, warning that private capital will only flow into markets that offer deep predictability and clear institutional structures.

title: Central Bank urged to probe into overseas transfers linked to Rs. 13bn NDB fraud
byline: The Central Bank has come under pressure to explain how funds involved in the Rs. 13 billion fraud at the National Development Bank (NDB) were transferred overseas, an opposition MP said yesterday.

title: Speaker confronts Opposition MPs over supplementary questions
byline: Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne today confronted Opposition MPs over raising supplementary questions where he accused them of violating Standing Orders.

title: SL’s LNG plans under fire as plants cost $50m a year in standby mode
byline: Sri Lanka’s plans to expand liquefied natural gas (LNG)-based power generation is facing criticism due to high costs, delays in infrastructure, and continued use of diesel fuel. Environmental groups and energy experts say that because the country still does not have a LNG terminal, power plants built to run on LNG are currently operating on diesel.

title: Sri Lanka vulnerable to global energy shock, warns GPI 2026
byline: While Sri Lanka has made significant strides in domestic stabilisation following its 2022 fiscal crisis, a leading global evaluation warns that escalating geopolitical conflict in the Middle East poses a critical threat to the island nation’s financial survival.

title: Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga climbs to World No. 3 in Javelin Rankings
byline: Sri Lanka’s javelin sensation Rumesh Tharanga has achieved a historic milestone by surging to the third position in the latest Men’s Javelin Throw World Rankings, published by World Athletics.

title: Petition targets Trump over use of Japanese manga characters on social media
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump is facing growing backlash from Japan and fans of the country’s popular anime and manga characters over his use of them in his social media posts.

title: Sri Lanka’s university system handicapped with dearth of teachers
byline: Sri Lanka’s state university system is facing a critical shortage of academic staff that could compromise the quality of higher education and professional training, Prof. Prageeth Weerathunga, President of the Federation of University Teachers’ Associations (FUTA) has warned.

title: Death row inmate freed from a 30 year old murder case
byline: The Court of Appeal has acquitted a man who had been sentenced to death for a double murder committed over 30 years ago, ruling that serious doubts existed regarding the reliability of the identification evidence relied upon by the prosecution.

title: Three Indian sailors missing after US says it hit tanker in Gulf of Oman
byline: The US military has disabled an oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman that it accused of violating an American blockade by ’’attempting to transport oil from Iran’’.

title: Kuwait closes airspace, diverts flights amid Iran attacks
byline: Kuwait temporarily closed its airspace early Thursday and diverted flights to alternative airports as a precautionary measure amid escalating regional tensions following Iranian attacks.

title: Dehiwala beach access routes to be officially named today
byline: A series of environmental conservation programmes aimed at protecting Sri Lanka’s coastal ecosystem will be held today (11) along the Dehiwala–Mount Lavinia coastline to mark World Environment Day.

title: ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026 Schedule: Full Fixtures, Match Timings in Sri Lankan Time
byline: The ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026 takes centre stage in England from June 12 to July 5, with 12 teams competing for the biggest prize in women’s T20 cricket. For fans in Sri Lanka, all match timings below are listed in Sri Lanka Standard Time (SLST).

title: Iran says it struck ships in Strait of Hormuz after US launches new strikes
byline: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) says it has struck ships in the Strait of Hormuz, after the US military launched a new wave of strikes on Iran.

title: Iran announces closure of Strait of Hormuz after US attacks
byline: Iran’s top ​joint military ‌command announced the closure ​of ​the Strait of ⁠Hormuz ​on Thursday, ​including oil tankers and commercial ​ships, ​saying any vessel ‌that ⁠will attempt passage will ​be ​shot ⁠at.

title: Over 2,000 cases filed during three-day Dengue campaign
byline: A total of 2,400 legal cases have been filed against individuals and institutions found maintaining dengue mosquito breeding sites during the special three-day dengue prevention programme conducted from June 8 to 10, health authorities said.

title: Kuwait reopens airspace, airport returns to normal operations after Iran attacks
byline: Kuwait resumes air traffic and Kuwait International Airport returned to normal operations after a temporary suspension prompted by Iranian attacks, the civil aviation authority says.

title: Communist Party expresses concerns over Sallay’s prolonged detention
byline: The Communist Party of Sri Lanka (CPSL) expresses deep concern over the continued detention of former Intelligence Chief Major General (retd.) Suresh Sallay, who was arrested on February 25, and has now been held for 95 days under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), according to a statement from it.

title: High Court rejects Shashi Weerawansa’s appeal, affirms sentence
byline: Colombo High Court Judge Manjula Thilakaratne dismissed an appeal filed by Shashi Weerawansa challenging the two year prison sentence and fine imposed on her for possessing an irregularly obtained passport.

title: Sajith raises concerns over delay in appointing judges to SC, CA
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa today raised concerns about the government’s failure to appoint four judges each to the Supreme Court (SC) and the Court of Appeal (CA), which had been vacant for more than six months.

title: Japan donates Rs. 200 Mn refrigerated truck fleet to boost fish distribution
byline: The Government of Japan has donated six refrigerated trucks valued at Rs. 200 million to Sri Lanka’s Ministry of Fisheries, strengthening the distribution network of the Ceylon Fisheries Corporation (CFC) and supporting efforts to reduce post-harvest fish losses.

title: Dengue cases surge as 5,000 patients reported in just 10 days
byline: Sri Lanka has recorded more than 5,000 dengue cases within the past 10 days, raising concerns among health authorities about the growing pressure on the country’s healthcare system.

title: Sri Lanka mulls seawater for drinking needs amid drought fears
byline: Sri Lanka may be forced to purify and distribute seawater for drinking purposes if a forecasted severe El Niño event leads to a prolonged drought and depletes the country’s main water sources, the Disaster Management Centre (DMC) warned.

title: Uva province records highest number of malnourished children under five- survey reveals
byline: A recent survey has revealed that the majority of children under five years of age suffering from malnutrition in the country are from the Uva province.

title: Bus conductor dies after suspected drug packet bursts inside stomach
byline: A bus conductor employed on a private passenger bus operating between Tangalle and Makumbura on the Southern Expressway has died after a packet of suspected narcotics reportedly burst inside his stomach, police said.

title: Is the govt.‘s claim that “fuel worth Rs. 720 is being sold for Rs. 433” actually true?
byline: Some government representatives have claimed that fuel is being provided to the public in Sri Lanka at a significantly reduced price compared to global market rates, arguing that fuel which should be sold at around Rs. 720 per litre is instead being sold for approximately Rs. 433 per litre.

title: Women’s T20 World Cup 2026
byline: The 2026 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup will be the tenth edition of the event scheduled to be hosted by the England and Wales Cricket Board from June 12 to July 5, 2026.

title: Sri Lanka's LNG plans under fire as plants cost $50m a year in standby mode
byline: Sri Lanka’s plans to expand liquefied natural gas (LNG)-based power generation is facing criticism due to high costs, delays in infrastructure, and continued use of diesel fuel. Environmental groups and energy experts say that because the country still does not have a LNG terminal, power plants built to run on LNG are currently operating on diesel.

title: SLAF conducts first test flight of upgraded Kfir C12 fighter aircraft
byline: The Sri Lanka Air Force (SLAF) today successfully conducted the first test flight of its upgraded Kfir C12 fighter aircraft at SLAF Base Katunayake, marking a major milestone in the modernization of the country’s fighter fleet.

title: Twelve police officers injured on second night of unrest in Northern Ireland
byline: Twelve police officers were injured and 16 arrests were made in the second night of unrest in Northern Ireland following the Belfast knife attack, Northern Ireland Secretary Hilary Benn has said.

title: Over 30 public officials arrested over bribery charges during first four months
byline: A total of 32 state officials and public servants have been arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) during the first four months of 2026.

title: Rough seas warning for coastal waters
byline: The Meteorology Department has warned of rough to very rough sea conditions around several coastal areas over the next 24 hours, urging naval and fishing communities to exercise extreme caution.

title: SriLankan Airlines expands connectivity across Saudi Arabia through new partnerships
byline: SriLankan Airlines has announced strategic partnerships with Saudi Arabian carriers Saudia and Flynas, further strengthening air travel connectivity between Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka while expanding access to a wider range of destinations for passengers.

title: Five Dehiwala beach access roads formally named; Ocean Pool project planned
byline: Five public access roads leading to Dehiwala Beach were formally named today as part of a series of environmental conservation programmes held to mark World Environment Day, with authorities also announcing plans to construct safe sea-bathing pools around the country.

title: New National Mineral Policy comes into effect after 27 years
byline: Sri Lanka’s National Mineral Policy has been completely revised for the first time in 27 years and was presented to Parliament, Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Sunil Handunnetthi announced today.

title: Leading coffee shop fined Rs. 400,000 for consumer law violations
byline: The Bandarawela Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday (June 10) imposed a fine of Rs. 400,000 on Barista Coffee Lanka (Pvt) Ltd, operating as Barista Express in Bandarawela, after the company pleaded guilty to four charges related to violations of consumer protection laws.

title: President chairs high-level meeting on El Niño preparedness
byline: A discussion to assess the potential impacts of the anticipated El Niño phenomenon and the preparedness measures of relevant institutions was held this morning (11) at the Presidential Secretariat under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

title: Two Indian seafarers killed in US attack on oil tanker
byline: Two Indian seafarers have died and one remains missing after a US attack on the Settebello oil tanker off the coast of Oman on Tuesday night, local news outlet The Hindu reports.

title: US and Iran exchange strikes across Middle East for second day in a row
byline: The US and Iran have exchanged strikes across the Middle East for a second consecutive day, further straining a shaky ceasefire agreed between the two countries in April.

title: Sri Lankan rupee edges lower against USD
byline: The Sri Lankan Rupee depreciated slightly against the US Dollar today (11) compared to Wednesday, with both buying and selling rates showing a marginal increase, according to the Central Bank of Sri Lanka.

title: El Niño under way and threatens weather extremes, scientists say
byline: El Niño - the natural Pacific weather pattern that pushes up global temperatures - has officially begun, US scientists say.

title: CSE extends decline as middle east concerns weigh on investor confidence
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) extended its losses on Thursday, with both benchmark indices closing lower as escalating tensions in the Middle East continued to dampen investor sentiment. Persistent geopolitical uncertainty and concerns over its potential economic implications kept investors on the sidelines, resulting in subdued trading activity and broad-based selling pressure across the market.

title: Coroner arrested in Ragama over Rs. 100,000 bribe
byline: A Coroner attached to the Ragama (North Colombo) Teaching Hospital has been arrested by investigative officers of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC).

title: UK defence minister quits, plunging PM Starmer deeper into leadership crisis
byline: British defence ​minister John Healey quit on Thursday in a dispute over military spending, accusing Prime Minister Keir Starmer of failing to commit the resources that are needed ‌to keep the country safe from heightened threats.

title: Trump says US will hit Iran ’very hard tonight’, wants control of energy infrastructure
byline: President Donald Trump said on Thursday the United States would hit Iran ’’very hard tonight’’ and wanted at some point to take Iran’s oil infrastructure hub Kharg Island, after tit-for-tat strikes ​in the Gulf undermined a shaky ceasefire.

title: Owner of fire-gutted elders’ home granted bail
byline: The Horana Magistrate’s Court today (11) ordered the release on bail of the owner of the ’’Mawpiya Sewana Senehase Kädella’’ elders’ home in Batagoda, Horana, who had been arrested and remanded in custody following a recent fire at the facility.

title: India says US hit another ship off Oman, confirms 3 dead in separate attack
byline: Three Indian sailors are confirmed killed as the country reports a separate incident involving a vessel ⁠⁠off Shinas port in Oman, the third attack linked to the United States this week.

title: MRIA investment project EOI deadline extended until July 9
byline: The deadline for submitting Expressions of Interest (EOIs) for the “Project of Investments to Utilize Resources of Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport (MRIA)” has been extended until July 9, 2026, offering prospective investors additional time to participate in one of Sri Lanka’s key aviation development initiatives.

title: ’System change’ promise unfulfilled, says Stalin
byline: Ceylon Teachers’ Union (CTU) General Secretary Joseph Stalin has alleged that the present government, despite coming to power promising systemic change, is no different from previous administrations when it comes to the education sector.

title: SLPP’s Cassilingam urges for better Jaffna train timings to improve connectivity
byline: While welcoming the resumption of the long-awaited Colombo–Jaffna train services, Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) Jaffna District Organizer Geethanath Cassilingam has urged authorities to address concerns over inconvenient train schedules and difficulties faced by the public in obtaining tickets.

title: UN humanitarian plan for cyclone Ditwah concludes, reaches 575,000 people
byline: The United Nations’ Humanitarian Priorities Plan (HPP) launched to assist communities affected by Cyclone Ditwah was officially concluded at a ceremony held in Colombo this morning (11), attended by Commissioner General of Essential Services and Chief of Staff to the President Prabath Chandrakeerthi and United Nations Resident Coordinator in Sri Lanka Marc-André Franche.

title: Illegal canned fish factory raided in Arachchikattuwa
byline: A canned fish manufacturing facility operating without the required licence from the Sri Lanka Standards Institute (SLSI) was raided in Arachchikattuwa today (June 11).

title: Faiszer Musthapha acknowledged by world-renowned artist
byline: Sri Lankan-born international entertainer Alston Koch has expressed gratitude to former Minister Faiszer Musthapha for the support extended to him during his efforts to promote Sri Lanka on the global stage.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026: 10 Best Group Stage Matches to Watch in Sri Lanka
byline: With 104 matches spread across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, most group stage kickoffs fall in the early hours of the morning in Sri Lankan Standard Time. You cannot watch everything, so the question becomes: which matches are worth setting the alarm for?

title: Health Ministry warns of silent health threat from everyday plastic use
byline: The Health Ministry has issued a strong warning over the growing use of non-standard plastic utensils and food containers, cautioning that long-term exposure could lead to serious health complications.

title: Middle East conflict sends global growth to lowest rate since COVID-19
byline: The conflict in the Middle East is expected to slow global growth to the lowest rate since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic amid higher energy prices, steeper inflation, and increased borrowing costs, according to the World Bank Group’s latest Global Economic Prospects report.

title: Multiple Pentagon floors locked down, evacuated due to ‘hazardous materials incident’
byline: Multiple floors and corridors inside the Pentagon have been locked down and others are being evacuated due to a “hazardous materials incident,” three sources familiar and the local fire department said.

title: From almost non-existent two nations to the high and mighty… Biggest World Cup Blasts Off
byline: The best, biggest and most looked forward to football World Cup kicked off in Mexico City today as renowned singer Shakira struck the vocal cords with the official song titled Dai Dai, an Italian expression meaning “come on, come on” after which the host Mexico played against South Africa in the curtain raiser. As many as 11 cities will also host matches in the USA with Canada showcasing two host cities and Mexico three.

title: Schools rugby league heats up in week 2
byline: The 2026 Schools Rugby League Tournament moves into its second round this weekend, with several blockbuster encounters set to light up the Division ‘A’ competition.
